claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
The tested Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a solidified, single-phase solid solution.
Removing Co increases lattice resistance or lattice friction against dislocation glide.
Low temperature reduces thermal activation of dislocation motion.
High strain rates hinder or challenge dislocation glide in the Co-free alloy.
Hindered dislocation motion increases the propensity for deformation twinning.
At low temperature and high strain rate, the Co-free alloy crosses over from predominantly dislocation slip to deformation twinning.
Deformation twinning enables the Co-free alloy to retain a favorable combination of strength and ductility.
Under matched low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions, the Co-free alloy will have a higher deformation-twin density than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under matched low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions, the Co-free alloy will have a higher yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Under matched low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions, the Co-free alloy will retain ductility comparable to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At high temperatures or very low strain rates, the Co-free alloy may revert to predominantly dislocation-based deformation.
The exact twin-density and yield-strength differences are not established by prior numerical data.
A controlled comparison must test the Co-free and equiatomic alloys under identical temperatures and strain rates and measure yield strength, elongation, and twin density.

Failure to observe a statistically significant increase in both twin density and corresponding yield strength in the Co-free alloy under low-temperature, high-strain-rate conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
